answer:
The included Videos application is **Celluloid**, the GTK front end for **mpv**. Try the file there, or open it with mpv to see its diagnostic output:
```
mpv <video-file>
```
If playback fails, keep the error message and identify the file's format. A player, decoder, graphics-driver or file problem needs that evidence; the presence of a codec package alone does not prove that this particular file will play.

You don't need to — media codecs are already installed. InterGenOS bundles the complete GStreamer stack (base, good, bad, ugly, and gst-libav/ffmpeg), so the popular audio/video formats work in the default players with nothing to add. If a particular file won't play, it's usually the file or an unusual format rather than a missing codec.

triggers: how do I change my wallpaper
answer: Right-click the desktop and choose "Change Background", or open GNOME Settings → Appearance → Background. InterGenOS ships its own wallpaper set (the default plus Helix, Overwatch, and Pulse), and you can pick any image of your own with the "Add Picture" button.

triggers: how do I enable dark mode
answer: InterGenOS already defaults to dark mode. To change it, open GNOME Settings → Appearance and choose Dark, Light, or Default under "Style". (This sets `org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme`, which apps follow automatically.)

triggers: how do I change the theme
answer:
Use **GNOME Tweaks** to choose icon and cursor themes. The first-boot **Welcomer** also offers the curated appearance choices.

The documented defaults are the InterGenOS icons and the Bibata-Modern-Classic cursor. Papirus-Dark and Cybernetic Blue are available icon alternatives. The GTK4 baseline is Adwaita with the distribution's defaults; icon and cursor choices are separate from an application's light/dark appearance.

triggers: how do I change the default application for pdfs
answer: In Files (Nautilus), right-click a PDF → Properties → "Open With" tab, choose your preferred app (Evince/Document Viewer is the default and is installed) and click "Set as Default". That app then opens all PDFs.

triggers: how do I set a custom keyboard shortcut
answer: Open GNOME Settings → Keyboard → "View and Customize Shortcuts" → scroll to the bottom → "Custom Shortcuts" → "+". Give it a name, the command to run, and press the key combination you want. You can also rebind any built-in shortcut from that same screen.

triggers: how do I change the timezone
answer: Open GNOME Settings → System → Date & Time. Turn on "Automatic Time Zone" to set it by location, or turn it off and pick your zone on the map / from the list.

triggers: how do I change the keyboard layout
answer: Open GNOME Settings → Keyboard → "Input Sources", click "+" to add a layout, and it appears in the top-right menu so you can switch (Super+Space cycles between them). Removing the extras leaves just your chosen layout.
